data.name: Piemonte
data.summary: Piemonte: no regional difference for the family's taxes. Capital gains, dividends and interest of a private investor taxed at the 26% imposta sostitutiva (or withholding as final tax), IVAFE, IVIE and inheritance tax are national and identical in this region. The regional IRPEF surcharge (addizionale regionale, 1.23% base rate, raised by many regions) and the municipal surcharge apply only to income in the progressive IRPEF base (reddito complessivo, art. 50 D.Lgs. 446/1997), not to investment income under the 26% substitute tax; they matter only for salary, pension or other ordinary income.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Worldwide taxation. Financial income (dividends, interest, capital gains) is taxed separately at a 26% substitute tax (12.5% on Italian and white-list government bonds), not at progressive IRPEF rates (23-43% plus regional/municipal surcharges).
regimes.eligibility: Italian tax residence: for more than 183 days (fractions counted) physical presence, habitual abode or domicile (centre of personal and family relationships) in Italy, or registration in the resident population register.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains on financial assets (listed or unlisted shares, including qualified holdings, bonds, funds) are subject to a 26% substitute tax. Gains on Italian and white-list government bonds 12.5%. Crypto-asset gains 33% from 2026. Real estate gains are exempt if held more than 5 years (or principal residence for most of the holding period); otherwise progressive IRPEF or 26% substitute tax.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Real estate held over 5 years: exempt.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Gains on government bonds 12.5%. Capital losses carried forward 4 years against gains (not against dividends). Exit tax not applicable to individuals' portfolios. Announced, not yet applicable: D.Lgs. 19 June 2026 n. 117 (new Testo unico delle imposte sui redditi, 377 articles; G.U. n. 132 of 3 July 2026, S.O. 26) applies from 1 Jan 2027 and repeals arts. 1-191 of the current TUIR (DPR 917/1986). It is a consolidation: commentators say the old provisions were carried over without changing their wording or rates except for coordination. The new article numbers (e.g. for art. 24-bis), and whether the 26% substitute tax (D.Lgs. 461/1997) and IVAFE/IVIE (DL 201/2011) are moved into it, were not confirmed. 2026 law is scored.

components.notes: 0.4% for assets in privileged-tax states (Switzerland excluded from 2024). Bank accounts: flat EUR 34.20 each. Italian-custodied securities pay a 0.2% stamp duty instead (not verified).

components.notes: Base: foreign cadastral value in EU/EEA, otherwise cost or market value. Not due if under EUR 200. Foreign property tax credited.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: IMU on Italian real estate: 0.86% basic rate on cadastral-based value for non-main homes (municipal variation); principal residence exempt except luxury categories (0.5%). Plus TARI waste tax.

inheritance.summary: Inheritance and gift tax (D.Lgs. 346/1990 as amended by D.Lgs. 139/2024): spouses and direct-line relatives, including children, pay 4% on the value above EUR 1 million per beneficiary. Gifts use the same rates and allowance. Self-assessment from 1 Jan 2025. If the deceased was Italian resident, worldwide assets are taxed. Italian real estate also bears mortgage (2%) and cadastral (1%) taxes, flat EUR 200 each if the heir claims first-home relief.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: EUR 1,000,000 per child (applies cumulatively to gifts and inheritance from the same donor).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Transfers of family businesses/controlling holdings to descendants exempt if control is held for 5 years. Italian government bonds exempt from inheritance tax.

regimes.name: Lump-sum tax for new residents (Art. 24-bis TUIR)
regimes.description: Optional substitute tax on all foreign-source income: EUR 300,000 per tax period for individuals transferring residence to Italy from 1 Jan 2026 (art. 24-bis(2) TUIR as amended by L. 199/2025; EUR 200,000 for transfers from 11 Aug 2024, EUR 100,000 before). Each included family member pays EUR 50,000. Replaces income tax on foreign income and gains (except gains on qualified holdings realised in the first 5 tax periods), IVAFE and IVIE, and foreign asset reporting. Italian-source income taxed normally. Ceases 15 years after the first tax period of validity (art. 24-bis(4)); revocable. During the option, inheritance and gift tax on transfers by the opting person is due only on assets located in Italy (art. 1(158) L. 232/2016).
regimes.eligibility: Not Italian tax resident for at least 9 of the 10 tax periods before the option takes effect (art. 24-bis(1)). The option is exercised after a favourable answer to a ruling request (interpello) to the Agenzia delle Entrate, filed by the deadline of the return for the year of transfer, and must state the last jurisdictions of tax residence (art. 24-bis(3)). Non-EU nationals need a visa (e.g. elective residence or investor visa).

lump_sum.notes: For residence transfers from 1 Jan 2026 (Budget Law 2026). Family members: EUR 50,000 each. Family of five = EUR 300,000 + 4 x EUR 50,000 = EUR 500,000 a year. Not covered: gains on qualified participations sold in the first 5 tax years (26%).

capital_gains.summary: Foreign gains covered by the lump sum, except gains on qualified (substantial) participations realised in the first 5 years, which are taxed at 26%. Italian gains taxed at 26%.

regimes.name: Family holding company (S.r.l.) with participation exemption
regimes.description: The family holds its listed shares through an Italian S.r.l. (IRES 24%). Dividends are 95% excluded from IRES (art. 89 TUIR) and gains on shares are 95% exempt (PEX, art. 87 TUIR) if held 12 months, booked as financial fixed assets in the first balance sheet and issued by a company outside privileged-tax states: 1.2% effective, with no minimum stake. The 2026 Budget Law (L. 199/2025, art. 1 c. 51-55) had limited both to stakes of 5% or EUR 500,000; art. 11 DL 38/2026 (converted by L. 88/2026) repealed those limits with effect from 1 January 2026. The holding must pass the non-operating company test (presumed revenue 1% of the securities' value, three-year average); a low-yield portfolio that fails pays IRES at 34.5% on at least a deemed 0.75% of that value. Bonds, funds/ETFs and shares sold within 12 months are taxed at the full 24%, so the advantage covers only the directly held shares kept as a long-term book. Payouts bear 26%. Inheritance is unchanged (4% above EUR 1m per child).
regimes.eligibility: Any Italian resident can form an S.r.l. (capital from EUR 1; EUR 10,000 for the ordinary form). Contributing securities to the company is a disposal at market value for the individual (gains taxed at 26%), so it suits cash or recently bought assets. Not usable together with the art. 24-bis flat-tax regime for foreign income.
regimes.duration_note: A holding vehicle has no statutory time limit; it lasts as long as the family keeps it and stays resident, subject to changes in the law.

structure.entity: S.r.l. (società a responsabilità limitata) family holding
structure.payout_notes: Dividends to resident individuals bear a 26% final withholding regardless of stake size (since 2018). Distributions are presumed to come from profits before capital reserves; repayment of capital contributions is tax-free once profit reserves are exhausted. Shareholder loans to the company can be repaid tax-free.
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: Non-operating company rules (società di comodo, art. 30 L. 724/1994, coefficients as amended by art. 20 D.Lgs. 192/2024 from tax year 2024): the company is non-operating if its average revenues and ordinary income items of the year and the two before fall below 1% of the average value of securities and shareholdings (plus 3% for buildings, 15% for other fixed assets). Then income is at least 0.75% of the securities' value, and IRES rises by 10.5 points to 34.5% on the whole taxable income; losses only offset income above the minimum, VAT credits are frozen and a minimum IRAP base applies. The exclusion for listed companies covers only listed companies, their subsidiaries and companies that CONTROL a listed company, not holders of small listed stakes. A EUR 30m share portfolio yielding 1.5-2% in dividends (EUR 450,000-600,000) passes the EUR 300,000 presumed-revenue test; a low-dividend growth portfolio may not, and whether PEX gains count as revenue was not confirmed. A disapplication ruling (interpello, c. 4-bis) is possible for objective circumstances. PEX (art. 87 TUIR, read 2026-10-15): 12 months' uninterrupted holding; classification as financial fixed assets (immobilizzazioni finanziarie) in the first balance sheet closed during the holding period; issuer not resident in a privileged-tax state (art. 47-bis) since the first period of holding, unless shown otherwise by ruling; the commercial-activity test does not apply to companies listed on regulated markets (c. 4). Losses on PEX shares are not deductible. Shares booked as current assets, or rotated within 12 months, are fully taxable at 24%. Dividends from privileged-tax states are fully taxable. IRAP: if shareholdings exceed 50% of assets the company is a non-financial holding (art. 162-bis TUIR) taxed under art. 6 c. 9 D.Lgs. 446/1997 (production value plus net interest, at regional rates up to about 5.6%), but dividends and share gains are excluded from the IRAP base, so a passive share holding usually has a nil IRAP base; bond interest would be included. General anti-abuse rule art. 10-bis L. 212/2000. A new consolidated TUIR (D.Lgs. 117/2026) replaces the TUIR and art. 30 L. 724/1994 from 1 January 2027.
structure.exit_and_liquidation: Italy has no exit tax on individuals who emigrate; the company itself would face the art. 166 TUIR exit tax only if it moved its seat abroad. On liquidation, latent gains are taxed in the company (PEX applies to qualifying shares) and the surplus over contributed capital is taxed at 26% as a dividend.

capital_gains.summary: Gains on shares realised by an S.r.l. are 95% exempt under the participation exemption (art. 87 TUIR) if the shares were held 12 months, classified as financial fixed assets in the first balance sheet of the holding period, and the issuer is not in a privileged-tax state; the commercial-activity test does not apply to listed companies (art. 87 c. 4). No minimum stake: art. 11 DL 38/2026 (conv. L. 88/2026) abrogated art. 87 c. 1.1 and art. 1 c. 51-55 L. 199/2025 (the 5% / EUR 500,000 test) with effect from 1 January 2026. 5% x 24% IRES = 1.2%. The rate assumes a buy-and-hold book and that the company passes the non-operating company test; otherwise 34.5% applies to the taxable 5% (1.7%) and to a deemed minimum income.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: PEX: 95% exempt; 12 months' uninterrupted holding; financial fixed assets in the first balance sheet; issuer outside privileged-tax states since first holding period; commercial activity not required for listed issuers. No minimum stake or value from 1 Jan 2026.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Company subject to IRES (S.r.l./S.p.A.) in ordinary accounting. The directors must book the shares as long-term financial fixed assets; positions bought for trading are current assets and fully taxable.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Bonds, investment funds/ETFs (fund units are not shareholdings) and shares held under 12 months or booked as current assets: full 24% IRES (individuals pay 26%, 12.5% on government bonds). Losses on PEX shares are not deductible. Non-operating company: IRES 34.5% and a minimum income of 0.75% of the securities' value (art. 30 L. 724/1994; art. 2 c. 36-quinquies DL 138/2011). Real estate inside the company does not get the individual 5-year exemption.

Fund/ETF units outside PEX stated from general knowledge, not from an opened source.
Whether the Agenzia delle Entrate challenges financial-fixed-asset classification of an actively rebalanced minority portfolio was not researched; the scored 1.2% assumes a genuine buy-and-hold book.
Text of the conversion law L. 88/2026 changes to art. 11 not read (Normattiva shows art. 11 in force from 23 May 2026 with the 1 Jan 2026 start date).
capital_gains.rate_basis: Listed shares and a private business: 24% x 5% taxable = 1.2% (PEX), assuming the shares are held over 12 months as financial fixed assets and the company passes the non-operating test (a EUR 30m share book with a 1.5-2% dividend yield does). If it fails: 34.5% x 5% = 1.725% on gains, plus a deemed minimum income of 0.75% of portfolio value (about 0.26% of value a year at 34.5% if actual income is lower). Local real estate: 24% IRES + 3.9% IRAP = 27.9%. Bonds and funds would be 24%.
capital_gains.professional_trader: PEX depends on booking the shares as financial fixed assets and holding them 12 months, not on trading frequency; active rotation within 12 months or booking as current assets loses the exemption (24%).
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: 12 months uninterrupted, from the first day of the twelfth month before the sale (art. 87 c. 1 lett. a).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Same treatment for foreign shares unless the issuer is resident in a privileged-tax state (art. 47-bis TUIR), checked since the first holding period.

dividends.summary: 95% of dividends received by an S.r.l. are excluded from IRES (art. 89 c. 2 TUIR), with no minimum stake: art. 11 DL 38/2026 (conv. L. 88/2026) abrogated art. 89 c. 2.1 and the 5% / EUR 500,000 test of L. 199/2025 from 1 January 2026. 1.2% effective. Dividends from privileged-tax states are fully taxable. Foreign withholding is creditable only in proportion to the taxable 5%, so it is largely a final cost. Assumes the company passes the non-operating company test (otherwise 34.5% on the taxable part).

wealth_tax.important_exceptions: IVIE on foreign real estate still applies to property held personally.

income.name: Italy

income_tax.summary: National IRPEF is 23% to EUR 28,000, 33% to EUR 50,000 and 43% above. With the Lombardy regional surtax (1.23% to 1.73% by income) and the Milan municipal surtax (0.8%, exempt below EUR 23,000) the marginal rates in Milan are about 25% to 45.5%. Employees pay 9.19% pension contributions; the self-employed (Gestione Separata, VAT number, no other cover) pay 26.07% up to a cap of EUR 122,295.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Gestione Separata 2026 (PwC): 26.07% for VAT-number holders enrolled only there (24% if covered elsewhere), income ceiling EUR 122,295, minimum income for a contribution credit EUR 18,808. Under the forfettario regime contributions are due on the deemed profit (revenue x 78% for professional services), so the effective rate on gross revenue is about 26.07% x 78% = 20.3% (not modelled in the rate field). Forfettario eligibility and rates are modelled as separate regimes below.
income_tax.local_tax_note: Brackets add the Lombardy regional surtax and the Milan municipal surtax (0.8%) to the national rate. Both surtaxes are in fact levied on the whole taxable income at the rate for the income band, not as marginal rates, so the combined figures are approximations. The Milan figure on the source page is the 2025 rate carried forward.

regimes.name: Digital nomad visa
regimes.description: Visa for non-EU highly qualified remote workers with annual income of about EUR 28,000 from foreign sources (three times the healthcare exemption threshold), six months of prior experience, a degree or equivalent experience, a one-year lease and EUR 30,000 of health cover. Consulates have accepted applications since 18 March 2026. The visa does not change tax: residents are taxed on worldwide income at the normal scale, with the forfettario or impatriati regimes as options.
regimes.duration_note: One year, renewable annually up to five years.

sources.title: Italy digital nomad visa complete guide 2026 (Remote Work Europe)

open_questions: Decree of 29 February 2024 (G.U. 4 April 2024) not opened and no Italian consulate or ministry page was reachable; the EUR 28,000 (three times the healthcare-exemption threshold), duration (1 year renewable to 5) and requirements rest on Remote Work Europe, which itself cites no links.
A dedicated nomad tax incentive was proposed but not enacted as of April 2026.

regimes.name: Impatriati regime (Legislative Decree 209/2023, art. 5)
regimes.description: Art. 5 D.Lgs. 209/2023 (Normattiva): employment, assimilated and SELF-EMPLOYMENT income (lavoro dipendente, assimilati e lavoro autonomo) produced in Italy counts for only 50% of taxable income (so 50% is exempt), up to EUR 600,000 a year, for five tax periods (arrival year plus four); the taxable share falls to 40% (60% exempt) with a minor child. Requires no Italian tax residence in the previous three periods (six or seven if working for the same employer or group), a commitment to stay resident for four years (benefit clawed back with interest otherwise), work mainly performed in Italy, and high qualification or specialisation. No Italian employer is required, so remote work from Italy for a foreign employer or foreign clients is covered by the text. Normattiva flags art. 5 as repealed by D.Lgs. 19 June 2026 n. 117 from 1 January 2027 (presumably moved into the new income-tax code); successor rules not opened.
regimes.duration_note: Five tax periods from the first year of residence.

regimes.name: Forfettario flat-tax regime for sole traders (15% on 78% of revenue)
regimes.description: Legge 190/2014 art. 1 commi 54-89 (Normattiva): sole traders and professionals with revenue up to EUR 85,000 pay a 15% substitute tax on deemed profit instead of IRPEF, surtaxes and IRAP; the regime ends in the year revenue exceeds EUR 100,000. Deemed profit = revenue x a coefficient set by ATECO code; for professional, scientific, technical and similar services the coefficient is 78% (Remote Work Europe; Allegato 4 not reached). Arithmetic: flat_rate on revenue = 15% x 78% = 11.7%, the value recorded in flat_rate (it is the rate on gross revenue). No deduction of actual expenses and no VAT charged. Social contributions are due on the deemed profit (about 20.3% of revenue at the 26.07% Gestione Separata rate). A tax resident nomad with revenue below EUR 85,000 can use it.
regimes.duration_note: Open-ended while revenue stays at or below EUR 85,000 (the regime ends the year revenue exceeds EUR 100,000 and the following year if above EUR 85,000).

open_questions: The 78% coefficient for professional services (Allegato 4) is from Remote Work Europe only; the Allegato was not reached on Normattiva. It depends on the activity's ATECO code.

Applies to the self-employed who are Italian tax residents; whether the nomad's foreign clients affect eligibility (none under the statute read) was not checked against Agenzia delle Entrate guidance.

regimes.name: Forfettario start-up rate (5% on 78% of revenue, first five years)
regimes.description: Same regime with a 5% substitute tax on deemed profit for the period the activity starts and the four following (art. 1 comma 65 L. 190/2014, Normattiva), if the person has not carried on a self-employed activity in the previous three years, the activity is not a mere continuation of a previous one, and, if it continues an activity of a third party, revenue is below EUR 85,000. Arithmetic: 5% x 78% = 3.9% of revenue. A newly arrived nomad starting a freelance activity in Italy can plausibly meet this; the conditions (a)-(c) of comma 65 were not read in full.
regimes.duration_note: Period in which the activity starts plus the four following periods; then 15% (11.7% of revenue).
